system.name: VLB (Vision-Language Bootstrapping)
system.one_liner: A dynamic multimodal evaluation protocol that bootstraps new visual question-answering samples from static benchmarks to cut data contamination and set complexity.

content.variant_note: panel (a) diagnoses data contamination on three concrete samples, panel (b) contrasts a static evaluation lane with a dynamic one that adds visual and linguistic dynamics
content.argues: Static benchmarks leak into training data and have fixed complexity; dynamic evaluation creates variants of them with flexible complexity.
content.subject: Evaluation images found inside a training-set ellipse, and a static versus a dynamic evaluation pipeline drawn as two lanes.

lessons.what_to_learn: Prove a hidden problem with concrete evidence: colour three leaked samples (dataset name, ellipse, dashed wedge, evaluation card with magnifier) inside a faded dataset ellipse, then give the fix as a static-versus-dynamic two-lane comparison with icon chains and an Easy-to-Hard arrow.
lessons.suits: benchmark and evaluation papers that must show leakage or overlap and then a remedy that generates variants of the benchmark.

evidence: some images in evaluation sets can be exactly found in the training set
dynamic evaluation can create various variants upon static benchmarks with flexible complexity
Once constructed, they are static with a fixed complexity

summary: This paper proposes Vision-Language Bootstrapping (VLB), a dynamic multimodal evaluation protocol that generates new visual question-answering variants from static benchmarks with flexible complexity and less data contamination. Figure 1 has two lettered panels. Panel (a), Data Contamination, puts three evaluation cards, from SEED-Bench, MME and MMBench, around a large ellipse of faded training datasets; each card's image and caption twin in the training set is highlighted yellow, pink or green and tied by a dashed wedge with a magnifier. Panel (b) stacks a static lane (Human, Internet Data, Static Benchmark, Fixed Complexity with a snowflake) against a dynamic lane where visual and linguistic dynamics turn a static benchmark into an easy-to-hard stack with Flexible Complexity and a flame.
summary_zh: 论文提出视觉语言自举（VLB），把静态多模态基准动态扩展成复杂度可调、数据污染更少的变体。图1(a)用三组颜色对应的卡片和虚线展示评测图片在训练集中有原样出现；(b)对比静态评测的固定复杂度与加入视觉、语言动态后由易到难的动态基准。
notes: Prior kinds kept (side-by-side-contrast problem-then-fix, concept-schematic); stage-pipeline added for the two icon-chain lanes in (b). The magnifier and dashed wedges look like a zoom callout but are used as a match link between twin samples, so zoom-callout is a loose fit. The snowflake and flame mark the state of complexity, not of a module. The orange text and outline colours of Flexible Complexity, Easy and Hard have no hex in the digest and are not in the palette.
